state.description: What every question needs: the evidence, the goal, the rule. Send only what the questions need. A file you name goes to the judge unread by you: name only what may go there. Text you did not write can steer the answer about it.

instructions.description: Name what to judge: the part of state in backticks (`ticket.text`), or `item`. Phrase it so a true answer is yes; one condition, no 'or'. No counting, arithmetic or date comparison: do those yourself.

criteria.description: choice: option names that say what they mean, each with a description. score: levels lowest first, each a situation on its own. noul (optional): true and false, each a concrete situation, not 'not X'.

questions.description: Each one judgment a person could make at a glance, literal and complete: Jev answers exactly what is written. A question without a type is a yes/no question. Pair a choice or a box with a noul asking whether anything fits. Or name a file of questions.

items.description: Things to ask the same questions about, each placed into each question; one row per item comes back, so you need not read them. An item can steer its own answer: read one before you act on it.

rank.description: With items: order rows by this question, highest first: a noul's yes, a choice's top option or `id.option`, a score's level. Without it, rows keep item order.

long_context.description: Use Jev's long context (262k tokens; slower and less accurate). Set it only when a reply said the request was too long for the default limits.

from.description: With items: a reply's next, passed back whole. It continues the same screen with the same model, and is refused if the state, the questions or the items changed.

questions.instructions: How soon does `ticket` need an answer?

examples.state: A ticket asks for a refund when it wants money back for a purchase.
